topic.title: The translation-index.xml Format
topic.shortdesc: Reference information for the elements, attributes, and layout rules used in the translation-index.xml file.

section.title: File Example
section.codeblock: <translation-index version="1"> <include href="publication-a.xml"/> <entry lang="de-DE"><source href="../../en/topics/install.dita" sha="b225cee9d0ca041bfd5765cb10165571e2250150"/><target href="../../de-DE/topics/install.dita" sha="08971eb314de5eecb3b299d064f96f1d4"/></entry> <entry lang="fr-FR"><source href="../../en/topics/install.dita" sha="b225cee9d0ca041bfd5765cb10165571e2250150"/><target href="../../fr-FR/topics/install.dita" sha="500c34a518243af8ef106ae1fd17dc4bc4543ef6"/></entry> </translation-index>

row.entry: Must be 1 for the current format.

section.title: Element: entry lang
section.p: One row per (language, source file) pair. The lang attribute is a BCP 47 language tag (for example fr, fr-FR, de-DE) and must match the tag you use for translation jobs.
Each entry contains exactly one <source> and one <target> child, written inline on the same line as the <entry>.

row.entry: Path to the source-language file and its Git blob SHA-1 at the time of the last recorded translation.
Path to the translated file and its Git blob SHA-1 at the time of the last recorded translation.

ul.li: Paths are relative to the index file's directory (not the workspace root), using POSIX / separators even on Windows.
Both source and target paths are required so you can copy the index together with translated files across branches or refactor folder layout without losing the pairing.
Paths must resolve to files inside the workspace.
Use one <entry> per line, and keep child elements inline. Do not use pretty-printed multiline entries.
Sort entries by lang, then by source href, within each file that contains entries.
The agent enforces this order when it writes the file. If you edit the file manually, following the same order helps reduce merge noise.

section.title: Element: include href
section.p: Optional. This element pulls in another index fragment from a path relative to the current file's directory. Use it in the following situations:

ul.li: Several product areas in one repository each maintain their own fragment.
You want one fragment per target language.
You want to keep the main index small to make reviews and conflict resolution easier.

By default, the agent appends new entries to the root index file. You can instruct it (in agent-instructions.md) to record entries for a given language or product area in a specific fragment instead. For example, "track French translations in .contentfusion/i18n/translation-index-fr.xml."
When the agent updates an existing entry, it edits the file where that entry is declared.

For entries stored in a separate fragment to be considered when the agent determines what is already translated in a later job, the root index must include that fragment with an <include>. If a fragment is written but not included, it is not consulted, so its files are detected as missing again in the next job.
Included files must exist. A missing include is an error.
